sections.overview: Cimberis attelaboides is a small, relatively primitive weevil associated with pines across Europe.
sections.identification: The adult has a narrow elongated snout, straight antennae and orange appendages; it is only a few millimetres long and can be confused with other snouted beetles.
sections.habitat: It occurs in lowland and mountain pine woods, where adults are found on pines during the warmer season.
sections.diet: Larvae feed in pollen-bearing male pine flowers, and adults are also associated with pine pollen.
sections.behavior: Adults are flower-visiting beetles seen on pines, especially during spring and early summer.
sections.reproduction: The documented life cycle links larval development to male pine flowers; detailed courtship or egg-laying behavior is not well covered in the sources consulted.
sections.ecology: This specialized pollen association connects the beetle closely to Pinus, especially Scots pine in British records; no other Cimberis profile in this catalogue is available for a species-by-species comparison.
sections.conservation: The sources consulted provide no formal species-level threat category, so local occurrence should not be mistaken for a global conservation assessment.
